description: Tuning layer for the boxing combo prototype. Temporary rules per docs/design/19_combat_prototype_implementation.md, not the final model. The full model lives in docs/design/22 through 32 and replaces this file as it lands.

rounds.note: A round is a fixed number of combo turns per docs/design/23_round_structure_and_judging.md. count * turnsPerRound must equal rules.maxTurns.

status.note: Prototype status model. The full model compares impact against effective_durability; here absolute damage stands in until fighter stats are wired into combat.
status.note_body: A body finish comes from accumulation, not an impact spike. Gating on the target being worn down as well as damaged avoids the all-or-nothing cliff that a pure impact threshold produced, and matches what body work actually does: drain first, finish second.

intervalRecovery.note: Between-round recovery. Larger than betweenRecovery and capped below full, per docs/design/23 section 3. The cap is expressed against rules.maxStamina and scales down with a fighter's own ceiling.

staminaCeiling.note: Stamina has a ceiling that only falls. Every recovery refills toward the ceiling and never past it, so being worn down is a permanent change to what a fighter can still do rather than a dip they breathe off. Spec: docs/design/38_stamina_attrition.md.
staminaCeiling.note_min: A floor is required or the loop feeds itself: a lower ceiling means gassing sooner, which lowers it again. The floor keeps a worn fighter dangerous instead of helpless.
staminaCeiling.note_tuning: bodyHitLoss barely moves the fixed-pattern table — 0.10 and 0.22 produce identical plan counts — because a fixed plan cannot exploit an opponent whose engine is shrinking. Its effect shows where it should: in the reactive-policy equilibrium, where lowguard went from never used to 13.7%.
staminaCeiling.note_threshold: Fraction of the fighter's own ceiling, not of rules.maxStamina. Someone already worn down is working while gassed at a lower absolute number, which is what being worn down means.

patterns.note: Fixed opponent plans. Replaced by the evaluation pipeline in docs/design/28_fighter_plan_generation.md once it lands.

low_stamina_plan.note: Condition-driven recovery fallback, matching the survival_override idea in combat_ai.json.

subBeat.note: Impact position inside a slot. Priority is an outcome of timing, not a separate rule. Impacts within tolerance share a snapshot so a double KO stays reachable. Spec: docs/design/30 section 3.

range.note: Single gap scalar moved by the cards themselves. Spec: docs/design/22_combat_range_model.md.

firstStrike.note: A strictly earlier impact weakens the later one rather than erasing it. Only a KO cancels.

reveal.note: Budget shared by every equipped information card. Extra cards buy trigger coverage across situations, never more disclosure in one turn. Spec: docs/design/31_information_economy_and_placement.md.

fighterDefaults.note: Both sides start identical so wiring fighter stats into resolution changes nothing on its own. Per-profile stat tuning is a balance step, done in config, not a code change. reference is the Derived value that maps to a 1.0 multiplier.

statInfluence.note: How Effective Performance reaches Action Result. weight scales how far a capability ratio moves the outcome; failThreshold is the ratio below which a correctly chosen evasion can still fail.

modifiers.note_vulnerability: A gassed fighter absorbs worse: less braced, slower to roll with it. staminaFloor weakens what you throw; this deepens what you take. Both read absolute stamina, so a fallen ceiling compounds through this automatically. Measured: at 0.30 two further plans died (flicker, patient) because everything ends before it can be answered; 0.15 keeps the same plan count as with the mechanic switched off.
modifiers.note: Head work is the damage and KO path; body work is the attrition path. A body shot takes stamina, so an opponent who neglects body defence gradually cannot act: costs go unpaid, actions fail, guards break. This was briefly tuned down to 0.35 while chasing a body plan that won every fight, but that turned out to be the saturated-part scoring bug, and the lower value had quietly cost body work its identity.
modifiers.note_score: Judges reward clean head work over body work, which is why head scores higher. Body earns its place through the stamina it takes, not through points.
modifiers.note_leak: Per-card block leak. A long guard covers more time but blocks coarsely, so it leaks more per hit. Tuning cost alone produced a cliff: either the guard was affordable and total, or unaffordable and fatal.
modifiers.note_drain: Tuning this is a narrow band. At 0.35 body work took nothing worth noticing; at 0.7 body plans took roughly half the equilibrium and killed four cards. 0.5 leaves an opponent who ignores body defence visibly drained without making body the answer to everything.

style_cards.note: Style Skill Cards: conditional passive traits, not timeline placements. Spec: docs/design/31_information_economy_and_placement.md. Each must express a different axis, or it is not a choice.

angle.note: Off-angle is a lasting positional state, unlike the one-shot counter window from sway and weave. It is only earned against an opponent who is committed to something — an attack that the step slipped, or a guard they are holding. Against someone simply breathing there is nothing to step around: they would just turn with you. And a hook follows you into the direction you stepped, so it is not evaded and lands harder than an ordinary mistimed evasion.
